problem:
Determine the dimension of the image of the map:
\[ H^{1}(G_{S}, Ad(\bar{\rho})) = H^{1}(G_{S}, \mathbb{F}_{p}) \oplus H^{1}(G_{S}, Ad^{0}(\bar{\rho})) \rightarrow H^{1}(I_{p}, Ad^{0}(\bar{\rho})) \rightarrow H^{1}(I_{p}, \mathbb{F}_{p}(\omega^{k-1})) \]
where \( Ad^{0}(\bar{\rho}) \cong \mathbb{F}_{p} \oplus \mathbb{F}_{p}(\omega^{k-1}) \oplus \mathbb{F}_{p}(\omega^{1-k}) \) as an \( I_p \) module.

# Dimension of the Image of the Composite Map

## Setting Up the Problem

We need to determine the dimension of the image of the composite map:
$$H^1(G_S, Ad(\bar{\rho})) \xrightarrow{\text{res}_{I_p}} H^1(I_p, Ad^0(\bar{\rho})) \xrightarrow{\text{proj}} H^1(I_p, \mathbb{F}_p(\omega^{k-1}))$$

where $Ad^0(\bar{\rho}) \cong \mathbb{F}_p \oplus \mathbb{F}_p(\omega^{k-1}) \oplus \mathbb{F}_p(\omega^{1-k})$ as an $I_p$-module.

## Decomposing the Source

Since $Ad(\bar{\rho}) = \mathbb{F}_p \oplus Ad^0(\bar{\rho})$, the source decomposes as:
$$H^1(G_S, Ad(\bar{\rho})) = H^1(G_S, \mathbb{F}_p) \oplus H^1(G_S, Ad^0(\bar{\rho}))$$

**First summand:** Under restriction to $I_p$, $H^1(G_S, \mathbb{F}_p) \to H^1(I_p, \mathbb{F}_p)$, and the projection to the $\mathbb{F}_p(\omega^{k-1})$ summand sends this to **zero** (different Galois modules).

**Second summand:** Under restriction, $H^1(G_S, Ad^0(\bar{\rho})) \to H^1(I_p, Ad^0(\bar{\rho})) = H^1(I_p, \mathbb{F}_p) \oplus H^1(I_p, \mathbb{F}_p(\omega^{k-1})) \oplus H^1(I_p, \mathbb{F}_p(\omega^{1-k}))$, and the projection extracts the middle component.

## Analyzing the Image via Inflation-Restriction

The key computation uses the inflation-restriction sequence for $1 \to P_p \to I_p \to T_p \to 1$:

$$0 \to H^1(T_p, \mathbb{F}_p(\omega^{k-1})) \to H^1(I_p, \mathbb{F}_p(\omega^{k-1})) \to H^1(P_p, \mathbb{F}_p(\omega^{k-1}))^{T_p}$$

Since $\omega$ is trivial on the wild inertia $P_p$ (as $P_p$ is a pro-$p$ group and $|\mathbb{F}_p^*| = p-1$ is prime to $p$), the action on $\mathbb{F}_p(\omega^{k-1})$ factors through the tame quotient $T_p \cong \widehat{\mathbb{Z}}'$.

## Determining the Image Dimension

The restriction map from $H^1(G_S, Ad^0(\bar{\rho}))$ to $H^1(I_p, \mathbb{F}_p(\omega^{k-1}))$ has its image determined by the **unipotent direction** of the inertia action. Specifically:

- The global cohomology classes in $H^1(G_S, Ad^0(\bar{\rho}))$, when restricted to $I_p$, can only produce a **single independent direction** in the $\mathbb{F}_p(\omega^{k-1})$-isotypic component.
- This direction corresponds to the universal extension class arising from the specific $I_p$-module structure of $Ad^0(\bar{\rho})$, encoding how the $\mathbb{F}_p(\omega^{k-1})$ weight interacts with the trivial weight under inertia.
- The tame inertia contribution $H^1(T_p, \mathbb{F}_p(\omega^{k-1}))$ contributes at most one dimension (the unique non-trivial homomorphism from $T_p$ to $\mathbb{F}_p(\omega^{k-1})$ compatible with the $\omega^{k-1}$-action), and the global-to-local restriction surjects onto precisely this 1-dimensional subspace.

## Conclusion

The image of the composite map is generated by a single cohomology class, corresponding to the unique non-trivial restriction direction in the $\mathbb{F}_p(\omega^{k-1})$ component.

$$\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p}\,\text{Im} = \boxed{1}$$
